title: Minimum speed at A
description: Essential: Student must state or use that at the highest point of the first loop (A), the critical condition for staying on track is mg = mv_A²/R₁.

title: Energy conservation for part (1)
description: Important: Student must apply conservation of mechanical energy from O to A to relate v₀ and v_A, correctly accounting for the 2R₁ height gain.

title: Final answer for part (1)
description: Essential: Student must obtain v₀_min = 6 m/s for the ball to stay on the OAB track.

title: Energy conservation for part (2)
description: Important: Student must apply conservation of mechanical energy from O to B to find the speed at B, given v₀ = 6 m/s and the height difference R₂.

title: Force analysis at B
description: Important: Student must apply Newton's second law at point B (lowest point of second loop) to find the normal force from the track: F_N - mg = mv_B²/R₂.

title: Final answer for part (2)
description: Essential: Student must state the pressure magnitude on the track at B as 6 N (equal to the normal force by Newton's third law).

title: Work-energy for part (3)
description: Important: Student must apply the work-energy theorem from O to C, accounting for friction on BC and the change in gravitational potential energy from O to B.

title: Final answer for part (3)
description: Essential: Student must obtain v₀_min = 8 m/s for the ball to reach and fall into the pit at C.

title: Sign or direction error
description: Pitfall: Student incorrectly assigns sign to work done by friction or misapplies the direction of normal force at point B.

title: Unit omission or mismatch
description: Pitfall: Student fails to include units in final answers or uses inconsistent units (e.g., cm instead of m) in calculations.
